sections.h2: Who records deeds and mortgages in Manatee County?
sections.html:
In Manatee County the clerk of court doubles as Official Recorder. Deeds, mortgages, liens, leases and payoffs all land at the Recording department in Bradenton, where staff scan each item, log the filing time, add it to the Official Records book and index it by name.

Walk-in filing is at 1115 Manatee Avenue West, Bradenton, FL 34205, the same street address used for overnight couriers. Ordinary mail travels to a post office box: Recording, P.O. Box 25400, Bradenton, FL 34206. Phone 941-741-4045.

Section 28.222 lists what the clerk files, from deeds and claims of lien to lis pendens notices, judgments and discharge certificates. For a seller three groups matter most: the deed proving title, the mortgage and payoff trail, and any lien or judgment that could stall a closing.

sections.h2: What are the ways to file a document with the Manatee County clerk?
sections.html:
There are three ways: bring the original in person, mail it with fees and a self-addressed envelope, or submit it electronically through an approved e-recording vendor. A mailed document is recorded the day it arrives, and the clerk asks for 3 to 5 business days after that for its return.

  • Counter: originals are handed back that day.
  • Post: send fees and a stamped return envelope, with the check payable to Clerk of Circuit Court.
  • E-recording: the original stays with you and the recorded image returns electronically. Deeds, mortgages, assignments and satisfactions travel this way most.

Legal forms and drafting help are outside the clerk's role, which points owners to an attorney or title company. Section 689.01 asks for a written conveyance signed before two witnesses. Any fix to an existing deed, whether a name added, a name dropped or a transfer to a trust or LLC, takes a brand new recorded deed.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Manatee County?
sections.html:
Using the clerk's own Notice of Commencement example, a typical instrument costs $10.00 for page one and $8.50 for each further page. That total lines up with s. 28.24: a base of $5.00 then $4.00, a modernization fee of $1.00 then $0.50, and a $4 technology fee on every page.

Common Manatee County recording charges, from the clerk's FAQ and Florida statutes

Names beyond the fourth add $1.00 each under s. 28.24(13). The clerk's fee calculator gives an exact total for your page count. A veteran recording a DD-214 pays nothing because veterans services is billed.

sections.h2: Who pays document stamp tax on a Manatee County deed?
sections.html:
Liability falls on every party, whichever side agrees to pay, with payment made through the clerk as the deed is recorded. Manatee County follows the standard Florida rate, 70 cents on each $100 of consideration.

Consideration counts cash, a discharged debt and any mortgage on the property, assumed or not. State revenue officials treat warranty, quit claim and life estate deeds, among others, as taxable and say estate planning transfers have no dedicated exemption; a personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable.

The clerk sends tax-due questions to the Department of Revenue at 850-488-6800. Under s. 201.02(7), a spousal homestead deed funded only by a mortgage and a divorce deed for the marital home are exempt.

sections.h2: How do you search Manatee County Official Records?
sections.html:
The clerk's website hosts a free Official Records search, and you can print your own deed or payoff for nothing. A certified copy runs $1.00 a page plus $2.00 for the certification, ordered through Public Access at 941-741-4040.

Records go back to the 1850s, and documents recorded before 1978 are held in the Historical Records Library at 941-741-4070. Plat maps as far back as 1887 can be viewed through the clerk's plat search. Land surveys are not recorded with the clerk, so ask the surveyor or the mortgage holder.

  • Not shown on public websites under s. 28.2221: military discharges, death certificates, and family, juvenile and probate case documents.
  • Death certificates and family, juvenile and probate documents can be viewed after registering a free account.
  • Military discharges are not viewable online, and only the person named may buy copies.

Owners can also sign up for the clerk's free Property Alert, an email whenever a document under a registered name is recorded, which costs nothing and can flag an unexpected lien or a fraudulent deed.

sections.h2: What should Manatee sellers confirm in the records before listing?
sections.html:
Confirm that a paid-off mortgage shows a recorded satisfaction, that no lien or judgment sits under your name, and that your deed is complete. After payoff the lender should record a satisfaction or release, and copies become available once it posts.

Owners usually get the original deed at closing from the seller or title company, and a lost one can be replaced with a recorded copy. A will is filed only after death, through Probate at 941-741-4025, a point that matters for an inherited house.

A Declaration of Domicile can be recorded with the clerk, yet the homestead exemption itself is requested from the Property Appraiser at ManateePAO.gov or 941-748-8208, with Florida's March 1 filing deadline.

sections.h2: What else does the Manatee County clerk record for owners?
sections.html:
Beyond deeds, the clerk records Notices of Commencement for building permits, Declarations of Domicile, liens and military discharges. The Notice of Commencement form comes from the building department that issued the permit, and the clerk lists its common charges as $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each additional page, a $1.00 per page certified copy fee with a $2.00 certification, and notary service at $5.00 for the first notarization and $2.50 for each added one.

Notary service is available at the clerk's office if you bring the completed, unsigned form and valid ID. Liens are governed by Florida Statute 713, and the clerk advises an attorney for questions. A Declaration of Domicile can be signed before a notary or in front of a deputy clerk at the Recording department, and it can be mailed or recorded in person.

Documents recorded from 1978 onward can be requested for a DD-214 only by the person named, who must come to the Recording department with photo ID. Anyone else should contact Manatee County Veterans Services at 941-749-3030.

sections.h2: Who lives in Manatee County, and what are homes worth?
sections.html:
Manatee County has grown 17.1 percent since the 2020 count, reaching an estimated 468,200 people across 743 square miles.

Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show homes worth a median $391,400 where owners live in them, 74.3 percent of 243,784 housing units occupied by their owners, rent at $1,671 and household income at $78,457. People 65 and over are 29.4 percent of the county, and builders pulled 11,015 permits in 2025. With growth like that, order the title search early to leave time for any recorded surprises.

faqs.q: Which Manatee County office takes deeds for recording?
faqs.a: At the clerk's Recording department, 1115 Manatee Avenue West in Bradenton, by post, or through an approved e-recording vendor. Questions go to 941-741-4045.

faqs.q: What are the recording charges in Manatee County?
faqs.a: The clerk's printed example is $10.00 for page one and $8.50 for each later page, with stamp tax on top where it applies. The fee calculator gives exact totals.

faqs.q: How long are Manatee County records kept online?
faqs.a: The archive starts in the 1850s, with anything recorded before 1978 held at the Historical Records Library. Military discharges and death certificates do not appear on public websites.

faqs.q: Can the clerk fix a mistake on my recorded deed?
faqs.a: Not by editing it. Corrections, name changes and trust transfers each need a new recorded deed, and the clerk cannot give legal advice.

faqs.q: Is document stamp tax owed on a Manatee County sale?
faqs.a: Usually. A deed carries 70 cents per $100 of consideration, all parties are liable, and the contract normally says who pays.
